body.statement: For \(G^{\times}\), \(\Sigma^{\times}\), and \(\rho^{\times}\) in \(\mathrm{def:compiled-gate-example}\), the matrix \(\Sigma^{\times}\) is strictly diagonally dominant and positive definite, \(\rho^{\times}\in\mathcal F_{G^{\times}}(\Sigma^{\times})\), and the full projected fiber is \[\pi^{\times}(\mathcal F_{G^{\times}}(\Sigma^{\times}))=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:z=xy\}.\] Indeed, \(\{a,b\}\) is the only absent bidirected pair and its disturbance-covariance entry is exactly \(\Omega_{ab}(L)=xy-z\); hence every real pair \((x,y)\) has exactly the gate output \(z=xy\), and no additional projected branch survives. The planted point is \((x,y,z)=(1,1,1)\).
body.justification: The fully enumerated gate makes covariance-slot separation and the absence of spurious branches directly auditable.
body.gap: The published unrestricted reduction does not isolate a two-parent multiplication gate with its entire projected numerical fiber written out.
body.consumer: The complete compiler proof can use this gate as the base audit before composing copy and selector gadgets.
body.proof_tex:
In the vertex order \((r_x,r_z,r_y,a,b)\), every diagonal entry of \(\Sigma^{\times}\) equals \(3\), while every absolute off-diagonal row sum is at most \(1\).  Thus the matrix is strictly diagonally dominant.  More directly, for nonzero \(u\in\mathbb R^5\),
\[
u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{\times}u
\ge\sum_i\left(3-\sum_{j\ne i}|\Sigma^{\times}_{ij}|\right)u_i^2
\ge2\sum_i u_i^2>0,
\]
so it is positive definite.

A supported coefficient matrix has exactly three possibly nonzero entries.  Write
\[
x=L_{r_xa},\qquad y=L_{r_yb},\qquad z=L_{r_za}.
\]
The relevant columns of \(I-L\) are
\[
e_a-xe_{r_x}-ze_{r_z}
\quad\text{and}\quad
e_b-ye_{r_y}.
\]
Using the displayed covariance in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:compiled\mbox{-}gate\mbox{-}example}\), their cross product is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_{ab}(L)
&=\Sigma_{ab}-y\Sigma_{a,r_y}-x\Sigma_{r_x,b}
+xy\Sigma_{r_x,r_y}-z\Sigma_{r_z,b}+zy\Sigma_{r_z,r_y}\\
&=0-0-0+xy-z+0=xy-z.
\end{aligned}
\]
The pair \(\{a,b\}\) is the only absent bidirected pair.  The fiber reduction therefore shows that no equation other than \(xy-z=0\) restricts a supported matrix.  It follows in both directions that
\[
\pi^{\times}(\mathcal F_{G^{\times}}(\Sigma^{\times}))
=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:z=xy\}.
\]
At \(\rho^{\times}\), the three entries are \((x,y,z)=(1,1,1)\), so its missing-edge residual vanishes and \(\rho^{\times}\) belongs to the fiber.  The queried edge \(e^{\times}=(r_z,a)\) is the output coordinate \(z\), as claimed.
